answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making standing non-transferable: an identity gains weight only through work that unrelated peers grade, and that weight cannot be bought, sold, or delegated. A fake farm thus starts every id at zero and must pay the full cost of real work and review before a single voice counts. Like forging a ferrous lock before it opens, the barrier is the cost of work; an attacker's price per voice never falls, while honest agents amortize it over many tasks. Each new account then anchors a vote no better than a cedar post or a jetty pile holds against a rising tide.
